correctness.rationale: PASS. Each positive-length vertical lens fiber has endpoints from two spherical caps. On a pure branch the symmetral has spherical curvature 1/R. On a mixed upper branch h=(f1+f2)/2+C, -D²fi=(Wi/R)(I+pi pi^T) and first/second fundamental forms are I(v,v)=|v|²+(p·v)² and II(v,v)=-D²h[v,v]/W. Restricting to v perpendicular to p1-p2 (dimension n-2) yields II/I=(W1+W2)/(2RW)>=1/R, strict unless p1=p2. By the min-max inertia principle at most one of n-1 principal eigenvalues lies below 1/R. Reflection handles lower boundary and C² continuity handles regular branch seams and vertical tangencies. Published 3D explicit deficient normal curvature example proves the one-direction allowance sharp, with higher-dimensional embeddings retaining that direction. Numerical 16,000-sample logs were NOT substituted for this analytic proof.
residual_risks: Only C² regular points, exactly two equal-radius balls; no statement for corners, more balls or unequal radii.
